entities.label: Sensorama
entities.blurb: Morton Heilig's coin-operated arcade cabinet bathed one viewer in stereoscopic film, stereo sound, vibration, wind, and smells decades before the word 'virtual reality' existed.

entities.label: Sword of Damocles
entities.blurb: Ivan Sutherland's ceiling-mounted head-mounted display drew wireframe rooms that stayed put as your head turned, founding the entire HMD lineage.

entities.label: NASA VIEW

milestones.what: Scott Fisher founds the VIEW lab at NASA Ames

entities.blurb: NASA Ames' Virtual Interface Environment Workstation combined a wide-FOV LCD headset, glove input, and 3D audio into the template every later VR system copied.

entities.label: VPL DataGlove
entities.blurb: VPL's fiber-optic-sensed glove let a computer see your hand for the first time, and its patents trickled down to a Nintendo toy.

entities.label: VPL EyePhone
entities.blurb: The first commercially sold VR headset cost as much as a house and needed a quarter-million-dollar rig to drive it, but it made 'virtual reality' a product category.

entities.label: CAVE
entities.blurb: Instead of strapping a screen to your face, the CAVE turned a whole room into stereo projection surfaces, becoming the workhorse of scientific VR for decades.

entities.label: Virtuality
entities.blurb: Jonathan Waldern's arcade pods gave the 1990s public its first taste of networked, head-tracked VR at four dollars a pop.

entities.label: Sega VR
entities.blurb: Sega's $200 Genesis headset was announced with fanfare and killed amid motion-sickness worries, a ghost of the VR console generation that never came.

entities.label: Nintendo Virtual Boy

milestones.what: discontinued after under a million units

entities.blurb: Nintendo's red-and-black tabletop 'VR' flop became the industry's cautionary tale, chilling consumer VR investment for over a decade.

entities.label: Forte VFX1 Headgear
entities.blurb: The flip-visor VFX1 brought head-tracked Doom and Descent to mid-90s PCs, heroic and doomed at $695 with 263x230 pixels per eye.

entities.label: Virtual I/O i-glasses
entities.blurb: Virtual I/O's lightweight sunglasses-style HMD was the sleeker rival in the brief 1995 consumer headset skirmish before the whole category collapsed.

entities.label: Smartphone Panel & IMU Supply Chain
entities.blurb: The iPhone era made small high-density displays, MEMS motion sensors, and mobile SoCs absurdly cheap, quietly ending the VR winter by accident.

entities.label: Oculus Rift DK1
entities.blurb: A teenager's garage prototype built from a phone panel and hobbyist IMU raised $2.4M on Kickstarter and single-handedly restarted the VR industry.

entities.label: Oculus Rift DK2

milestones.what: adds positional tracking and low-persistence OLED

entities.blurb: DK2 added camera-based positional tracking and a low-persistence OLED that teardowns revealed to be a literal Galaxy Note 3 screen.

entities.label: Oculus Rift CV1
entities.blurb: The first consumer Rift opened the 2016 tethered VR wars with Touch controllers arriving months later to complete the package.

entities.label: HTC Vive
entities.blurb: The Valve-HTC alliance shipped room-scale VR with laser-swept Lighthouse tracking and made walking around a virtual room the new baseline.

entities.label: PlayStation VR
entities.blurb: Sony strapped VR onto 40 million PS4s with a headset tracked by a colored glowing orb, outselling its PC rivals on sheer install base.

entities.label: PlayStation VR2
entities.blurb: Sony's OLED-HDR sequel added inside-out tracking, eye tracking, and headset rumble, arriving into a market the standalone Quest already owned.

entities.label: Windows Mixed Reality

milestones.what: OEM headsets launch with Fall Creators Update

entities.blurb: Microsoft's OEM army of inside-out-tracked headsets undercut Rift and Vive on price, then was deprecated and deleted from Windows itself.

entities.label: Samsung Gear VR
entities.blurb: A Galaxy phone snapped into Oculus-powered goggles put millions of people into VR and then dead-ended when standalone headsets arrived.

entities.label: Google Cardboard
entities.blurb: A literal folded cardboard box with lenses gave tens of millions their first VR glimpse for a few dollars, both democratizing and cheapening the medium.

entities.label: Google Daydream
entities.blurb: Google's fabric-covered upgrade to Cardboard bet on phone-slot VR just as the industry pivoted to standalone headsets, and died in three years.

entities.label: Oculus Go
entities.blurb: The $199 phone-free headset proved standalone VR could be cheap and frictionless, even if its 3DoF tracking made it a transitional species.

entities.label: Oculus Quest
entities.blurb: The first Quest crammed full 6DoF room-scale VR into an untethered $399 box, and the entire industry's roadmap bent toward it.

entities.label: Meta Quest 2

milestones.what: rebranded from Oculus to Meta Quest 2

entities.blurb: At $299 the Quest 2 outsold every previous VR headset combined, making standalone VR the default and Facebook-login controversy the price of entry.

entities.label: Meta Quest 3
entities.blurb: Quest 3 pivoted the line toward color-passthrough mixed reality, landing months before Apple's Vision Pro at a tenth of the price.

entities.label: Valve Index

milestones.what: sells out on Half-Life: Alyx announcement

entities.blurb: Valve's own headset paired 144Hz displays with finger-tracking 'knuckles' controllers and sold out for months when Half-Life: Alyx was announced.

entities.label: Microsoft HoloLens
entities.blurb: The first untethered see-through holographic computer put spatially mapped AR on real faces, even if its postage-stamp field of view deflated the demos.

entities.label: Microsoft HoloLens 2

milestones.what: US Army IVAS contract worth up to $21.9B

entities.blurb: HoloLens 2 doubled the field of view, chased enterprise and a massive Army contract, then quietly became the end of Microsoft's headset line.

entities.label: Magic Leap One
entities.blurb: After years of whale-in-a-gym hype and billions raised, Magic Leap's lightwear goggles landed as a modest AR headset that sold a few thousand units.

entities.label: Apple Vision Pro
entities.blurb: Apple's $3,499 micro-OLED headset rebranded the field as 'spatial computing' and instantly reset expectations for passthrough quality and eye-hand input.

entities.label: OpenXR
entities.blurb: Khronos' royalty-free API ended the era of per-headset SDK lock-in, becoming the standards bridge nearly every surviving XR runtime crossed.

entities.label: VPL Research
entities.blurb: Jaron Lanier's startup was the first company to sell VR hardware, and its patent portfolio outlived it as the field's buried treasure.

entities.label: Sun Microsystems
entities.blurb: The workstation giant scooped up VPL's foundational VR patents in 1998, a footnote acquisition that ended the first VR era's intellectual estate.

entities.label: Oculus VR

milestones.what: brand retired in favor of Meta Quest

entities.blurb: Born from a Kickstarter and sold to Facebook for two billion dollars within two years, Oculus dragged VR out of its twenty-year winter before its own name was retired.

entities.label: Meta (Facebook)

milestones.what: renames itself Meta around the metaverse bet

entities.blurb: Facebook bet its very name on VR, pouring tens of billions into Reality Labs to own the headset platform it feared missing like mobile.

entities.label: Microsoft

milestones.what: winds down HoloLens and Windows MR

entities.blurb: Microsoft pioneered untethered AR with HoloLens and armed a fleet of Windows MR OEMs, then walked away from both fronts.

entities.label: Sony
entities.blurb: Sony is the only console maker to actually ship VR twice, riding the PlayStation install base where PC rivals had to sell whole rigs.

entities.label: Apple
entities.blurb: Apple waited out a decade of VR wars before entering with the Vision Pro and a vocabulary that pointedly never says 'virtual reality'.

entities.label: Google

milestones.what: launches Cardboard, invests in Magic Leap

entities.blurb: Google flooded the world with cardboard viewers, bankrolled Magic Leap, shipped Daydream, and then abandoned the whole VR experiment.

entities.label: Valve

milestones.what: unveils SteamVR and Lighthouse with HTC

entities.blurb: Valve's research lab gave modern VR its low-persistence displays, Lighthouse tracking, and the SteamVR platform everyone else's headsets plug into.

entities.label: HTC
entities.blurb: The fading phone maker bet its future on the Vive partnership with Valve and briefly owned the high end of VR.

entities.label: Samsung Electronics
entities.blurb: Samsung supplied the OLED panels inside early Rifts and turned its own phones into headsets with the Oculus-powered Gear VR.

entities.label: Nintendo
entities.blurb: Nintendo's Virtual Boy misadventure scarred the company so deeply it sat out VR until a cardboard Labo kit two decades later.

entities.label: Sega
entities.blurb: Sega hyped a consumer VR headset for the Genesis and then shelved it, one of the quiet retreats that defined the 90s VR bust.

entities.label: Magic Leap
entities.blurb: The most-funded startup in AR history raised billions on secrecy and whale demos, nearly collapsed, and reinvented itself as an enterprise vendor.

entities.label: Morton Heilig
entities.blurb: The cinematographer who dreamed of an 'experience theater' built the Sensorama alone and died before the industry he foreshadowed took off.

entities.label: Ivan Sutherland
entities.blurb: The father of computer graphics sketched 'The Ultimate Display' on paper in 1965 and then hung it from the ceiling in 1968.

entities.label: Bob Sproull
entities.blurb: Sutherland's student collaborator who helped build the Sword of Damocles went on to a storied career at PARC and Sun Labs.

entities.label: Scott Fisher
entities.blurb: The NASA Ames researcher whose VIEW lab wired gloves, headsets, and 3D audio into the first complete modern VR system.

entities.label: Jaron Lanier
entities.blurb: The dreadlocked polymath who popularized the term 'virtual reality' and sold the world its first VR gear through VPL.

entities.label: Carolina Cruz-Neira
entities.blurb: As a PhD student at EVL she co-invented the CAVE, then spent a career building room-scale VR facilities across academia.

entities.label: Jonathan Waldern
entities.blurb: The British VR PhD who founded W Industries and put Virtuality pods in arcades worldwide, two decades too soon.

entities.label: Palmer Luckey

milestones.what: departs Facebook; founds Anduril later that year

entities.blurb: The teenager who prototyped Rifts in his parents' garage restarted an industry, was pushed out of Facebook, and pivoted to defense tech with Anduril.

entities.label: John Carmack

milestones.what: resigns from Meta for AGI startup Keen

entities.blurb: The Doom engine legend lent Oculus instant credibility as CTO and spent a decade squeezing latency out of headsets before leaving Meta in frustration.

entities.label: Brendan Iribe

milestones.what: leaves Facebook amid PC VR strategy shift

entities.blurb: Oculus' co-founder and first CEO steered the company through Kickstarter and the Facebook sale before exiting as the PC Rift line wound down.
